title: Joint Venture Agreement
summary: Two parties team up on a specific project, sharing contributions, control and profits without merging their businesses.
useWhen: Two businesses or individuals want to pursue one defined project or opportunity together for a limited time.
watchOuts: An unincorporated joint venture is usually treated like a partnership. Each venturer can be liable for venture debts, and it may need to file a partnership tax return. Consider forming an LLC for the project.
If one party only contributes money and relies on the other's efforts for profit, the arrangement may be an 'investment contract' (a security). That can trigger securities law requirements.
Spell out who owns intellectual property and customer relationships created by the venture, and what each party may do after it ends.
Antitrust: venturers who are competitors must not use the venture to fix prices or divide markets.

sections.title: 1. Parties and venture
sections.body:
**Venturer A:** {{party_a_name}}, {{party_a_address}} ({{party_a_email}})

**Venturer B:** {{party_b_name}}, {{party_b_address}} ({{party_b_email}})

The venturers agree to work together on the following project under the name {{venture_name}} (the "Venture"), starting on {{effective_date}}:

{{project}}

sections.title: 2. Contributions
3. Responsibilities
sections.body:
Venturer A will: {{roles_a}}

Venturer B will: {{roles_b}}

sections.title: 4. Decisions
sections.body: The venturers will make decisions together in good faith. Each must approve in writing any expense over {{spending_limit}}, any borrowing or guarantee, any contract binding the Venture for more than 90 days, any change to the project scope, and admitting another participant. Neither venturer may bind the other outside the Venture's approved activities.

sections.title: 5. Money and records
sections.body: Venture funds will be held in {{bank_account}}. Revenue goes into that account and approved expenses are paid from it. The venturers will keep complete records, share a written monthly statement of income and expenses, and allow each other to inspect the books on reasonable notice.

sections.title: 6. Profits and losses
sections.body: Net profit is Venture revenue minus approved Venture expenses. Net profits and losses are shared: Venturer A {{split_a}}%, Venturer B {{split_b}}%. Distributions are made quarterly, after reasonable reserves.

sections.title: 7. Return of capital first
sections.body: Before profits are split, distributions first repay each venturer's cash contributions, in proportion to the unreturned amounts.

sections.title: 8. Intellectual property
sections.body: Each venturer keeps ownership of what it brings to the Venture and grants the Venture a non-exclusive license to use it for the project only. Work product created for the Venture is jointly owned in the profit-sharing percentages, unless the venturers agree otherwise in writing. Neither may license or sell jointly owned work product without the other's consent.

sections.title: 9. Exclusivity
sections.body: While the Venture runs, neither venturer will pursue the same project with a third party.

sections.title: 10. Confidentiality
sections.body: Each venturer will keep the other's and the Venture's non-public information confidential and use it only for the Venture, during the Venture and for three years after.

sections.title: 11. Relationship and liability
sections.body: The Venture is limited to the project described. Nothing else creates a general partnership, agency or employment between the venturers. Each venturer is responsible for its own taxes on its share of profits. Each venturer will indemnify the other for losses caused by its own negligence, misconduct or breach. The venturers will cooperate on any required tax filings for the Venture.

sections.title: 12. Ending the Venture
sections.body: The Venture ends {{end_condition}}, or earlier by written agreement, or if one venturer materially breaches and does not cure within 30 days after notice. When it ends, the venturers will finish or wind down open work, collect receivables, pay Venture debts, return unused contributed property, and distribute any remaining funds as described above.

sections.title: 13. Disputes
sections.body: The venturers will first try to resolve disputes by negotiation, then by mediation, before litigation.

sections.title: 14. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.
